name: FFmpeg Sequential Word Drawtext Chain
use_when: A short hook, lyric-style line, or word-by-word caption test needs to be generated directly in FFmpeg.
The number of words is small enough for a labeled filter chain to stay readable.
The agent has reliable word or phrase timing data.
avoid_when: The caption sequence is long enough that many drawtext nodes would be brittle.
The line requires rich caption layout, per-word collision avoidance, or spring motion.
The generated filter graph cannot be logged and regenerated from data.

timeline_pattern.pattern: token_timing_data -> word_or_phrase_windows -> drawtext_word_1[label1] -> drawtext_word_2[label2] -> ... -> final_output -> contact_sheet_qc
timeline_pattern.chain_rule: Each drawtext consumes the previous labeled video stream and outputs a new label.
timeline_pattern.window_rule: Each word or phrase has its own enable window derived from transcript or beat timing.
timeline_pattern.fallback_rule: Switch to ASS subtitles, Remotion, or pre-rendered overlays when the chain gets long.

motion.rule: Use simple timed appearances or fades; avoid trying to recreate complex kinetic typography through a huge drawtext chain.

keyframe_values.short_window: Word windows around 0.3-0.6 seconds can work for fast social reveal tests if the words remain readable.
keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: Word starts should align to transcript timing or the intended beat within a few frames.
keyframe_values.split_threshold: If the chain becomes difficult to inspect, split the render into passes or switch tools.

sound.rule: Do not add per-word SFX by default; reserve sound cues for key impact words and keep speech clear.

captions.rule: Use phrase-complete chunks when one-word timing makes the sentence harder to understand.

color.rule: Use one consistent caption style unless a specific impact word needs a controlled accent.

implementation.ffmpeg: Generate a filter_complex chain from structured word/phrase timing; add optional alpha expressions per word only when the graph remains manageable.
implementation.remotion: Prefer a mapped array of word components with startFrame/endFrame and spring/fade props for longer or more animated word sequences.
implementation.blender: Use separate text strips or objects only for short generated title moments.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create separate text layers or caption compounds per word/phrase, then trim each to its spoken window.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use caption-to-graphics or Essential Graphics layers for selected word emphasis, not every long subtitle line.

common_mistakes: Generating a drawtext node for every word in a long video.
Using one-word chunks where phrase chunks would be clearer.
Failing to log the generated graph, making errors hard to debug.
Letting word timings lag behind speech.
Layering sequential words over faces, proof, UI, or captions.
qc: Word or phrase windows match transcript timing.
The filter graph is logged and can be regenerated.
Contact sheets show no collisions with faces/proof/UI/products/action.
Long sequences are split, rendered as ASS, or moved to Remotion before they become brittle.
Caption chunks remain readable and meaningful at phone size.
